brief.headline: The aluminium curve did not just stay in contango, it more than doubled it - and on the very same ring, every other base metal's front moved the opposite way, which turns a market-wide financing story into an aluminium-specific one.
bullets: WHAT MOVED: on Tuesday's LME official, aluminium cash settled $3,242.00 and three-month $3,264.00, so cash now sits $22.00 BELOW the forward - a contango that more than doubled from $10.50 the day before, and a complete reversal of the $21.00 premium for immediate metal that existed five sessions ago. The exchange has gone from paying to have metal now to paying more than twice as much to put it off.

WHY IT IS AN ALUMINIUM STORY AND NOT A MARKET STORY: on the identical session, copper's and zinc's fronts stayed in backwardation and merely narrowed, while nickel's and lead's contangos TIGHTENED. Four of the five base-metal fronts moved TOWARDS paying for immediate metal. Aluminium alone moved away from it. Rising financing costs should press every metal the same way; they plainly did not.

THE TENSION THAT WILL NOT GO AWAY: LME warehouse stock drew again, down 75 tonnes to 242,125 - a second straight draw and the third in four sessions, at a level close to multi-decade lows. Visible metal keeps being consumed while the front keeps getting looser. Something is repricing the cost of carrying aluminium that is not visible in the inventory line.

WHAT TO WATCH: three-month settled just $3.00 above 3,261, the narrowest margin of this entire sequence and the level that separates a consolidation from a break. Watch today's 13:20 London official for whether the contango widens a third time, and watch whether the two-day-old US-Iran negotiating track - talks the US publicly ties to a post-November timetable - produces anything operational on Gulf shipping.

lme.commentary: A SECOND PRE-REGISTERED TEST RESOLVED, AND IT RESOLVED THE SAME WAY AS THE FIRST. Yesterday this page published three outcomes for today's spread - the contango WIDENS, confirming a regime change at the front; it HOLDS near current levels; or it RETURNS TO BACKWARDATION BEYOND $15.00 - and named the third as the condition for restoring the bull case. IT WIDENED, AND BY MORE THAN A DOUBLING. On the 22-September official cash settled $3,242.00 against three-month $3,264.00, a $22.00 CONTANGO from $10.50. The six-session sequence now reads $21.00 backwardation, $18.50, $3.00, minus $10.50, minus $22.00. A single crossing could have been positioning noise; a crossing that deepens on the next settled official is a regime, and this page treats it as one. THE CROSS-METAL EVIDENCE IS THE MOST VALUABLE THING ON THE BOARD TODAY AND IT POINTS SOMEWHERE SPECIFIC. On the identical ring, copper's backwardation narrowed from $58.00 to $37.00 and STAYED a backwardation; zinc's narrowed from $87.00 to $68.00 and STAYED a backwardation; nickel's contango TIGHTENED from $140.00 to $130.00; lead's tightened from $38.00 to $26.50. Four of five fronts moved towards immediacy; aluminium moved $11.50 away from it. For several runs this page has leaned on a generic financing-cost explanation - real ten-year yields at 4.3-4.4% make a backwardation structurally expensive to sustain. THAT EXPLANATION IS WEAKER TODAY THAN IT WAS YESTERDAY, BECAUSE THE SAME FINANCING COST APPLIES TO COPPER AND ZINC AND THEIR FRONTS DID THE OPPOSITE. The honest position is that carry is a necessary condition and not a sufficient one, and that something aluminium-specific is doing the rest. THE STOCK LINE REFUSES TO COOPERATE WITH EITHER STORY. Visible LME stock drew a further 75 tonnes to 242,125, a second consecutive draw and the third in four sessions, roughly 9,090 tonnes below the August mean of 251,215 and close to multi-decade lows. Seventy-five tonnes is not a signal by itself and this page will not inflate it; the DIRECTION is the point, and the direction has been unchanged while the curve has travelled $43.00 in five sessions. THE FLAT PRICE FELL ON BOTH LEGS BUT UNEVENLY. Cash fell $20.50 or 0.63% and three-month $9.00 or 0.28%, so cash did more than twice the work for a second consecutive session - which is arithmetically how a contango deepens, and is also why the move cannot be dismissed as a forward-curve artefact. Cash closed BELOW the August monthly mean of $3,249.63 for the first time in this window. Unlike Monday, the currency channel is at least CONSISTENT this session: the LME euro fixing weakened to 1.14630 from 1.14900 and the dollar index rose, so a stronger dollar accompanied a lower dollar-priced metal. Consistency is not causation, and a currency move cannot explain the SPREAD at all, since it shifts both legs together. THE LEVEL THAT MATTERS IS NOW ALMOST TOUCHED. Three-month settled $3,264.00, just $3.00 above the 3,261 line this page has tracked for seven runs, having held above it on every session since 15-September. SMM's suggested core range for LME aluminium this week is $3,220-3,300, a band whose floor sits well below the level. A daily settlement beneath 3,261 is this page's published condition for raising the bear scenario further.

logistics.note: REVIEWED WEDNESDAY 23-SEPTEMBER-2026. THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL NEW PUBLIC INFORMATION THIS RUN IS DIPLOMATIC RATHER THAN OPERATIONAL, AND IT CUTS BOTH WAYS. SMM's 23-September summary records that on 22-September US President Trump, speaking at the 81st UN General Assembly, reiterated that the United States would reach an agreement with Iran AFTER THE NOVEMBER MIDTERM ELECTIONS; that Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi met US envoy Witkoff in New York and Trump described a three-hour meeting with the Iranian delegation as very productive with another to be arranged; and that Iran has publicly set CONDITIONS for reopening the Strait of Hormuz - immediate lifting of the maritime blockade, immediate unfreezing of all Iranian assets, and an end to the war on all regional fronts. READ THIS CAREFULLY RATHER THAN OPTIMISTICALLY. A negotiation is now visibly under way, which is the first genuine de-escalation signal of this cycle. But the publicly stated US timetable puts any agreement AFTER November, and Iran's stated conditions are maximalist. The transit constraint is therefore still in force today and is not publicly guided to clear inside this quarter. TREAT THESE AS REPORTED DIPLOMATIC STATEMENTS, NOT AS SETTLED OUTCOMES. WHY THE ARROW IS CUT FROM UP TO FLAT AND NOT TO DOWN: the direction of news has genuinely changed - talks are happening, are described by one party as productive, and a reopening condition set has been publicly articulated, which is more than existed at any point in this cycle. But NOTHING OPERATIONAL HAS CHANGED. The prior evidence stands unrefuted: Reuters tracking cited 20-September put daily commodity transits at 3-6 ships between 2 and 18 September against a normal ten-day average of 12-18, and a tanker was reportedly struck near Khasab, Oman on 18-September with the attribution still UNCONFIRMED. The second-order freight evidence also stands: SMM's 17-September bauxite weekly records Guinea-to-China ocean freight at around $39-42/wmt, a lane that never touches the Strait, because regional disruption withdraws tonnage from the global pool and reprices capacity everywhere. Flat is the honest arrow for a risk whose news flow improved and whose facts on the water did not.

headlines.title: THE CONTANGO MORE THAN DOUBLED ON A SECOND CONSECUTIVE OFFICIAL, WHICH TURNS A CROSSING INTO A REGIME. On the 22-September official cash settled $3,242.00 against three-month $3,264.00, so cash now sits $22.00 BELOW the forward, against $10.50 the session before and a $21.00 BACKWARDATION five sessions ago. This page published the three-way test in advance for a second time - widen, hold, or return to backwardation beyond $15.00 - and it widened. Cash fell $20.50 or 0.63% while three-month fell only $9.00 or 0.28%, so cash did more than twice the work for a second session, which is arithmetically how a contango deepens and is why this cannot be dismissed as a forward-curve artefact.

ALUMINIUM WAS THE ONLY METAL ON THE BOARD WHOSE FRONT LOOSENED, AND THAT IS THE MOST INFORMATIVE FACT AVAILABLE TODAY. On the identical 22-September ring copper's backwardation narrowed from $58.00 to $37.00 but held; zinc's narrowed from $87.00 to $68.00 and held; nickel's contango TIGHTENED from $140.00 to $130.00; lead's tightened from $38.00 to $26.50. Four of five fronts moved TOWARDS paying for immediate metal while aluminium moved $11.50 away from it. A rising-financing-cost story presses every front the same way. It did not. The generic carry explanation this page has leaned on for several runs is therefore weaker today, and something aluminium-specific is unaccounted for.

LME WAREHOUSE STOCK DREW FOR A SECOND CONSECUTIVE SESSION, WIDENING THE DISAGREEMENT WITH THE CURVE RATHER THAN RESOLVING IT. Visible stock fell 75 tonnes to 242,125 on the 22-September session, a third draw in four sessions, roughly 9,090 tonnes below the August monthly mean of 251,215 and close to multi-decade lows. Seventy-five tonnes is not a signal on its own and this page does not inflate it - the DIRECTION is the point, and it has been unchanged while the front travelled $43.00 in five sessions. Four of the five base-metal stock lines drew on the same ring, with lead drawing 3,025 tonnes and zinc 2,125.

A PUBLIC US-IRAN NEGOTIATING TRACK HAS OPENED FOR THE FIRST TIME THIS CYCLE - BUT THE STATED US TIMETABLE IS AFTER THE NOVEMBER MIDTERMS. SMM records that on 22-September President Trump, at the 81st UN General Assembly, reiterated the US would reach an agreement with Iran after the November midterm elections; that Foreign Minister Araghchi met US envoy Witkoff in New York with Trump describing a three-hour meeting as very productive and another to be arranged; and that Iran has publicly set conditions for reopening the Strait - immediate lifting of the maritime blockade, immediate unfreezing of all Iranian assets, and an end to the war on all regional fronts. Tagged bearish because any credible path to reopening removes a supply-risk premium; the conditions are maximalist and nothing operational has changed on the water.

ALBA'S RECOVERED CAPACITY IS CORROBORATED A THIRD TIME AT AROUND 1.3 MILLION TONNES, AND SMM EXPLICITLY FRAMES IT AS LIFTING EX-CHINA OPERATING CAPACITY. The 23-September summary states, citing foreign media, that Aluminium Bahrain's operating capacity has recovered to around 1.3 Mt, further lifting overseas operating capacity - the third separate public retelling of the same figure in six days without revision. This is the largest single tranche of recovered ex-China capacity in the public record this cycle. The counterweight remains live: CRU Group is reported as holding Gulf production down around 25% year on year, which cannot be fully reconciled with Alba at 1.3 Mt unless the shortfall sits overwhelmingly with EGA and Qatalum.

CHINESE INGOT DESTOCKING WIDENED INTO THE HOLIDAY AND THE NATIONAL TOTAL IS REPORTED BELOW 800,000 TONNES. SMM's 23-September summary records that as of Monday, China's social inventory of aluminium ingots fell 12,000 mt from the prior Thursday and 55,000 mt from the prior Monday, with destocking expected to continue near term. Separately, secondary aluminium ingot inventory across the three major consumption regions fell 283 mt to 12,403 mt on a widening spot-futures spread and pre-holiday stockpiling. THE ATTRIBUTION MATTERS AND SMM SUPPLIES IT: the widening draw is credited to a Xinjiang outbound shipment disruption combined with downstream stockpiling - both of which reverse by design after the 01-08 October holiday.

CHINESE PHYSICAL SPLIT SHARPLY BY REGION AGAIN, AND THE SPLIT IS THE SIGNAL. On 22-September central China transactions settled around a DISCOUNT of 70-90 yuan/mt to the SHFE October contract, with traders raising quotes but buying sentiment among purchasing traders and processors too weak to follow, so realised prices deviated significantly from offers. South China transacted at a PREMIUM of 210-250 yuan/mt on limited domestic arrivals and holders reluctant to sell, with some actively attempting to raise prices. SMM A00 spot traded between parity and a 20 yuan/mt premium to the October contract. A market this regionally divergent is one where logistics rather than consumption is setting the local price.

THE LIQUID-ALUMINIUM SHARE FELL AGAIN, WHICH IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC PROXY FOR REAL CHINESE CONSUMPTION ON THIS PAGE. SMM reports China's weekly aluminium production STABLE last week, but with some downstream sectors making production cuts that reduced liquid aluminium purchases, taking the liquid-aluminium proportion DOWN a further 0.02 percentage points. Liquid aluminium goes straight from the potline into a casting or extrusion operation without ever becoming an ingot; when its share falls, fabricators are consuming less. If consumption were genuinely accelerating into the holiday, this number would rise rather than fall. It has now fallen on consecutive readings while ingot inventory drew - which is exactly the pattern a logistics-driven draw produces.

THE ALUMINA PANEL GOT ITS FIRST NEW DATED PRINT IN EIGHT RUNS AND IT SAYS ALMOST NOTHING. SMM reports an 18-September deal at $354/mt FOB East Australia for 30,000 mt October shipment, with a 45,000 mt seller's-option leg at $357/mt. Against the 11-September trade of $353.50/mt for 50,000 mt that is plus $0.50/mt, or 0.14% over seven days - directionally up, economically trivial. The surrounding public commentary continues to describe spot alumina as stable with the supply-demand SURPLUS pattern unchanged and the ex-China premium steady at 312 yuan/mt. For the smelter margin the implication is unchanged: alumina is not the binding constraint, and a flat cost line against a falling exchange price compresses margin from the revenue side.

THE GUINEA-TO-CHINA BAUXITE CORRIDOR KEEPS WIDENING, WHICH IS A SLOW BEARISH FORCE ON THE UPSTREAM COST STACK. SMM reports that the 320,000-tonne Winning Ambition berthed at Yantai Port on 19-September carrying Guinean bauxite, the FOURTH time that port has set the global record for largest single-vessel bauxite discharge, and that Yantai has now received 82 bauxite vessels of the 300,000-tonne class. This is a throughput datum rather than a price, and this page does not use it to move any figure. Its analytical value is as a counterweight to the freight-cost story: ocean freight on this lane has been climbing on Middle East tension, yet corridor capacity is simultaneously being scaled.

THE DATED HIGH-LEVEL MACRO CATALYST IS NOW LIVE THIS WEEK. SMM's 23-September summary records that the Chinese and US heads of state are about to meet and that Chinese and US economic and trade lead officials held consultations in New York, lifting expectations for easing relations. Groundwork was laid on 20-September when Vice Premier He Lifeng held consultations with Treasury Secretary Bessent and Trade Representative Greer. FOR THIS MARKET THE RELEVANCE IS SPECIFIC RATHER THAN GENERAL: regional delivered prices are currently set by tariff policy rather than physical scarcity, so any movement on the trade file transmits straight into the premium complex. Market commentary already attributes part of recent support to expectations of easing, which makes disappointment a live risk in the same window.

CHINA NAMED ALUMINIUM AMONG THE SCARCE MINERALS IT WILL TARGET UNDER THE 15TH FIVE-YEAR PLAN. The Ministry of Natural Resources said on 23-September that rigid growth in demand for important mineral resources will continue, and set out a national geological mapping plan lifting 1:50,000 regional geological survey coverage on land to 51% and mineral surveys in important metallogenic belts to 66%, large-scale prospecting campaigns focused on oil, iron, copper and ALUMINIUM, about 300 energy and resource bases, and improvement of mining, beneficiation and comprehensive utilisation recovery rates. This is a long-dated resource-security signal, not a near-term supply one, and this page weights it accordingly.

AZERBAIJAN ANNOUNCED A NATIONAL MINING AND METALLURGY PROGRAMME TARGETING 100,000 t/y OF ALUMINIUM BY 2030. SMM reports the programme on 23-September. THE HONEST WEIGHT IS SMALL: 100,000 tonnes is roughly 0.14% of global primary output and 2030 sits beyond any forecast horizon carried on this page. It is recorded because the ex-China capacity pipeline is one of the two live disagreements here and announcements of this kind accumulate - Century and EGA's proposed $4bn, 750,000 t/y Oklahoma smelter, Hindalco's INR 210bn Odisha expansion adding 360,000 t/y, and EGA's DX+ Ultra licence to NALCO for a proposed 500,000 t/y Angul expansion are the larger entries on the same list.

CHINESE SCRAP CIRCULATION IS TIGHTENING FOR A REGULATORY REASON RATHER THAN A DEMAND ONE, AND THE PRESSURE IS SPREADING. SMM reports tax inspections in central China continuing to ESCALATE, with the resulting drop in regional scrap supply set to significantly disrupt circulation, and scarcity of compliant invoiced scrap continuing to rise. SMM A00 closed at 24,270 yuan/mt, down 50, while ADC12 held at 24,500 yuan/mt with only isolated 100 yuan/mt cuts, because tightening tax-invoice policy has raised compliant procurement costs and enterprises are unwilling to cut prices. Secondary ingot inventory across three regions fell 283 mt to 12,403 mt. Marginally supportive of primary demand, but the mechanism is a compliance squeeze, not consumption.

THE ENERGY COMPLEX HAS STOPPED FALLING HARD AND IS NOW DRIFTING, WHICH WEAKENS YESTERDAY'S CLEAN COST-FLOOR STORY. On the 22-September reference session Brent fell a FIFTH consecutive session but only 0.62%, to about $99.71, against 3.77% the day before; European gas TTF fell a second session, minus 1.83% to about EUR 71.91, against minus 7.90%. The gas move still transmits fastest, through European smelter power, and continues to relieve the two named gas exposures on this page - Alunorte's temporary terminal-access agreement with its gas supplier and Qatalum's curtailment at roughly 60% of 648 kt nameplate. THE CARBON SETTLEMENT CYCLE IS NOW SIX RUNS OVERDUE and the directional signpost for it is weaker than it looked yesterday.

earnings.note: Revenue RMB 11.53bn, up 32.4% year on year. Net profit attributable to owners RMB 2.30bn, up 166.1%. EPS RMB 1.11 against RMB 0.58 in the corresponding period of last year, up 91.4%. THE CLEANEST PUBLIC READ THIS WEEK ON HOW FAR SMELTER MARGIN HAS EXPANDED AT 2026 PRICES, AND IT COMES FROM AN INTEGRATED, SELF-SUPPLIED PRODUCER. The company operates 788,100 t/y of electrolytic aluminium capacity in Huolinguole, Inner Mongolia with a captive power plant, plus an alumina refining and aluminium hydroxide base in Binzhou, Shandong; it states that self-sufficiency in alumina and electricity fully meets its production requirements. Profit attributable rose 166% on revenue up 32%, which is operating leverage of roughly five times and is only possible when the price rises against a cost base that does not. Management attributes the gain to higher electrolytic aluminium selling prices, lower production cost from a rising green-energy share, and an optimised financing structure. TWO FORWARD DISCLOSURES MATTER BEYOND the quarter: 1,040 MW of wind and 110 MW of solar were commissioned by end-June with the programme roughly 66% complete and the green share expected to exceed 50%, which lowers the cost base further; and the 500,000 t/y integrated electrolytic aluminium project in Saudi Arabia, invested with partners in 2025, had completed all compliance approvals with on-site construction in full swing. That project is a dated, sourced addition to the non-Chinese capacity pipeline. THE UNCOMFORTABLE IMPLICATION FOR PRICE BULLS: margins this wide at the low end of the cost curve are exactly the condition that funds new capacity, and this disclosure shows the funding and the capacity in the same document.

Adjusted EBITDA Dh4.51bn, up 11% from Dh4.07bn, with the adjusted EBITDA margin widening to 33.3% from 27.0%. Profit rose on three named drivers - higher realised aluminium prices, stronger regional premiums and LOWER ALUMINA PRICES - while a third of the sales volume was simply unavailable. A 630 basis-point margin expansion on a 10% revenue decline is only possible when the cost side has fallen faster than the top line, and the alumina leg is the reason. IT ALSO EXPLAINS TODAY'S PRICE ACTION IN ONE LINE: the same release that showed the margin also showed the recovery date, and the market traded the recovery date. earnings.note: RECORD QUARTER ACROSS EVERY SEGMENT. Consolidated revenue RS 84,825cr, up 32% year-on-year; consolidated EBITDA RS 14,989cr, up 73%; net profit RS 7,013cr, up 75%. The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. The COPPER segment also set a record at RS 918cr, up 36%. NOVELIS, the downstream subsidiary, reported adjusted EBITDA of $516m, up 24% from $416m a year earlier and equivalent to RS 4,875cr (+37%), with net income of $164m (+71%) and adjusted EBITDA of roughly $563 per tonne, helped by the restart of the Oswego hot mill in early June 2026 and continued Bay Minette commissioning. THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. Revenue rose 32% while EBITDA rose 73% and upstream aluminium EBITDA rose 81% - operating leverage of well over two times on the upstream leg. The mechanism is integration: captive bauxite, captive alumina and captive coal-fired power insulate the cost stack from exactly the two legs that are currently rising for non-integrated smelters, namely seaborne bauxite (SMM index $71.57/mt, +$0.70 w/w) and seaborne alumina ($356/mt FOB East Australia on the 05-Aug trade). THE CONTRAST WITH CENTURY IS THE POINT. Century Aluminum, which buys its alumina, has now cited unfavourable raw-material price realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for two consecutive quarters; Hindalco, which makes its own, posted a record. Management had guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation into this quarter and still delivered a record, which says the LME move more than absorbed it. FOR THE MARKET VIEW: this is bullish for the margin narrative and neutral-to-bearish for the supply narrative, because producers earning at this level have every incentive to run flat out and to accelerate the restart pipeline.

Constellium reported Q2-2026 Adjusted EBITDA of $439 MILLION, a record, taking H1-2026 to $798m, and RAISED FULL-YEAR 2026 GUIDANCE to $980m-$1.020bn of Adjusted EBITDA EXCLUDING METAL PRICE LAG with free cash flow in excess of $300m. Leverage was 1.8x at the quarter end. Management states that the 2028 targets of $900m ex-lag EBITDA and $300m of free cash flow will now be met two years early. THE METAL PRICE LAG IS THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS FOR READING THIS PAGE and it is disclosed by the company: the $439m headline INCLUDES a $129m non-cash benefit from metal price lag, so the ex-lag figure is $310m. The four-quarter ex-lag path is $196m, $213m, $262m, $310m against headline figures of $235m, $280m, $359m and $439m - the gap between the two series has widened every quarter. THE READ-THROUGH IS THE MOST IMPORTANT ONE ON THIS PANEL FOR ANYONE TRYING TO SIZE HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 EARNINGS CYCLE IS REAL. Constellium is a converter, not a smelter: it buys primary and scrap and sells rolled and extruded product, so a rising LME shows up in its results as a NON-CASH metal price lag benefit before it shows up anywhere in the operating business. That lag contributed $126m across the whole of FY2025 and $226m in the FIRST HALF of 2026 alone - it has nearly doubled in half the time. UNDERLYING PERFORMANCE IS GENUINELY GOOD, with ex-lag Adjusted EBITDA up 58% from $196m in Q3-2025 to $310m in Q2-2026 and the company pulling its 2028 targets forward by two years - but a reader who takes the $439m headline as operating performance overstates it by 29%. THE GENERAL POINT EXTENDS ACROSS THIS WHOLE PANEL: a large share of the 2026 aluminium earnings recovery is price-lag and inventory revaluation rather than volume or spread, which is exactly the kind of earnings that reverses when the LME stops rising - and the completed August board, on which aluminium's monthly mean rose 2.97% against copper's 6.12% and zinc's 7.76%, is the first evidence that it may be about to.

Kaiser reported record Q2-2026 adjusted EBITDA of $166.3m against $67.7m a year earlier, a 146% increase, on net sales of $1.2566bn and conversion revenue of $437.0m. GAAP net income was $96.8m or $5.72 per diluted share against $23.2m and $1.41. Adjusted EBITDA margin on conversion revenue doubled to 38.1% from 18.1%. H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA was $294.8m against $141.1m. Net debt leverage improved to 2.1x from 3.4x at 31-December-2025 and the full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook was raised to +45-55% year on year from +20-30%. Shipments rose 6% to 305.7 million lbs, led by packaging at 155.8 million lbs and aerospace/high-strength at 60.8 million. THE READ-THROUGH IS A WARNING ABOUT HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 DOWNSTREAM EARNINGS CYCLE IS A PRICE ARTEFACT RATHER THAN A DEMAND ONE, AND KAISER DISCLOSES IT MORE HONESTLY THAN MOST. Adjusted EBITDA includes management-estimated FAVOURABLE METAL PRICE LAG of approximately $27.0m in Q2-2026 and $36.0m in Q1-2026 - $64.0m across the half against $36.0m in H1-2025. That is roughly 22% of H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA arising from the timing difference between the Midwest Transaction Price embedded in cost of sales and the market price over the period, not from conversion economics. MANAGEMENT SAID SO EXPLICITLY: the raised full-year outlook 'assumes a NEUTRAL metal price lag through the end of the year, and does not assume a continuation of the metal lag or consumption cost tailwinds recorded in the first half', and the CEO said the company expects aluminium price dynamics to normalise over the balance of the year. THE COMMERCIAL LESSON FOR READING THIS WHOLE PANEL: a rising aluminium price inflates downstream converter earnings twice - once through genuine mix and volume, once through inventory timing - and the second half reverses if the price stops rising. Kaiser's underlying story is nevertheless real: conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.43 from $1.30, packaging conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.12 from $0.92, and aerospace shipments grew as destocking eased. Both things are true at once and the filing quantifies the split, which is why this row is worth its place.

status.update: REFRESHED ON NEW DATED EVIDENCE THIS RUN, AND THE NEW EVIDENCE IS DOWNSTREAM RATHER THAN SMELTER-LEVEL. Analysis published 20-September on SMM data puts Chinese primary aluminium OPERATING capacity near 40.8 Mt against a 45 Mt government ceiling, and records alumina output rising 1.1% month on month in August as new Guangxi refineries ramp. Downstream, billet inventories eased to 152,500 tonnes on 17-September from a four-year seasonal high of 157,500 tonnes on 14-September, with Foshan alone holding 75,500 tonnes; billet processing fees rebounded across Foshan, Wuxi and Nanchang, two of them from below-cost territory; and the SMM A00 spot recovered RMB 200 or 0.83% to RMB 24,380/mt on 18-September after a roughly RMB 380/mt weekly fall. GUANGXI BILLET PRODUCERS BEGAN MAINTENANCE CURTAILMENTS IN THE WEEK OF 17-SEPTEMBER WITH NO TONNAGE OR DURATION DISCLOSED - an expectation, not a confirmed reduction, and flagged as such. The smelter-level picture is unchanged: August primary output a record 4 million tonnes, up 4.7% year on year, January-August about 31 Mt, up 3.9%, a pace annualising near 47 Mt; exports 626,000 tonnes in August and 4.67 Mt January-August, up 16.7%. The molten-aluminium ratio ran at 77-79% in August, so visible billet stocks understate total metal. NEW 23-SEPTEMBER: SMM reports China's weekly aluminium production STABLE last week, with some downstream sectors cutting production and the liquid-aluminium share edging DOWN a further 0.02 percentage points on reduced liquid purchases. Separately, China's Ministry of Natural Resources said on 23-September that the 15th Five-Year Plan will target scarce minerals including ALUMINIUM through a national geological mapping plan lifting 1:50,000 regional survey coverage to 51%, mineral surveys in key metallogenic belts to 66%, and about 300 energy and resource bases - a long-dated resource-security signal rather than a near-term supply one.

catalysts.text: TODAY'S LME OFFICIAL - THE THIRD READING OF THE SAME PRE-REGISTERED TEST, AND THE SINGLE MOST INFORMATIVE SCHEDULED EVENT ON THIS PAGE. The contango has now crossed and then MORE THAN DOUBLED, from $3.00 backwardation to minus $10.50 to minus $22.00 across three consecutive officials. THE QUESTION IS STATED IN ADVANCE AGAIN: does the contango WIDEN a third time, which would end any remaining argument that this is positioning noise; does it STABILISE near $20.00, which would make a new equilibrium the base case; or does it NARROW SHARPLY BACK TOWARDS FLAT, which would reopen the tightness reading? The published reversal condition is unchanged: a return to BACKWARDATION BEYOND $15.00 on a settled official restores the bull case towards 25%. Watch the stock line with equal attention - a third consecutive draw against a third consecutive widening would make the curve-versus-inventory disagreement the defining feature of this cycle.

THE 3,261 LEVEL IS ALL BUT TOUCHED. Three-month settled $3,264.00 on Tuesday, just $3.00 above it, having settled above it on every session since 15-September; the margin has narrowed from $12.00 to $3.00 in a single session. A daily settlement BELOW 3,261 is this page's published condition for raising the bear scenario beyond its new 33%, and on the weekly Elliott count it sits close to the level the position-degree structure turns on. SMM's suggested core range for LME aluminium this week is $3,220-3,300 - a band whose floor sits $41.00 BELOW the level, which is itself informative about how the market is framing the downside.

THE CHINA-US HEAD-OF-STATE MEETING IS NOW LIVE, AND IT IS THE BEST-DATED MACRO CATALYST ON THIS PAGE. SMM's 23-September summary records that the Chinese and US heads of state are about to meet and that economic and trade lead officials held consultations in New York, lifting expectations for easing relations; groundwork was laid on 20-September when Vice Premier He Lifeng met Treasury Secretary Bessent and Trade Representative Greer. FOR THIS MARKET THE RELEVANCE IS SPECIFIC RATHER THAN GENERAL: regional delivered prices are currently set by tariff policy rather than physical scarcity, so any movement on the trade file transmits directly into the premium complex. Market commentary already attributes part of aluminium's recent support to expectations of easing, which makes disappointment a live risk in the same window.

THE US-IRAN NEGOTIATING TRACK IS NOW PUBLIC AND DATED, AND IT IS THE SINGLE LARGEST POTENTIAL SUPPLY-SIDE REPRICING ON THE PAGE. Trump reiterated on 22-September at the UN General Assembly that the US would reach an agreement with Iran AFTER the November midterm elections; Araghchi met Witkoff in New York and Trump described a three-hour meeting as very productive with another to be arranged; Iran publicly set conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz - lifting the maritime blockade, unfreezing all Iranian assets, ending the war on all regional fronts. THE TIMETABLE IS THE KEY DETAIL AND IT IS WHY THIS IS NOT PRICED AS IMMINENT: a post-November US timetable places any agreement outside this quarter, and Iran's stated conditions are maximalist. Nothing operational has changed on the water. Treat as reported diplomatic statements, not settled outcomes.

THE MONTHLY CARBON-INPUT SETTLEMENT CYCLE IS OPEN, OVERDUE AND HAS STILL NOT PRINTED - A SIXTH CONSECUTIVE RUN. Prebaked anode, coal tar pitch and green petcoke marks normally settle around the 17th-18th of each month. Nothing has published, so roughly a fifth of the smelter cash-cost stack is carried on marks about a month old. THE DIRECTIONAL SIGNPOST WEAKENED THIS RUN RATHER THAN STRENGTHENING: Brent has fallen five consecutive sessions but the last was only 0.62%, against 3.77% the day before, and European gas fell 1.83% against 7.90%. The complex is drifting rather than collapsing, so the case for a sharply lower settlement is softer than it looked yesterday. This page will append a mark to the input histories only when a dated public figure exists.

THE NEXT DATED STEP IN THE US-CANADA TARIFF SCHEDULE: a US vehicle and dairy import ban takes effect, following Canada's 50% counter-tariffs across CAD 27.6bn in force since 08-September and the 08-September White House annex that lifted previously exempt downstream aluminium lines to a combined levy of up to 100%. THE CONTEXT REMAINS THE ONE THAT MAKES THIS DATE INTERESTING: on 22-September Novelis was reported to be cutting production and about 80 jobs at Kingston, Ontario explicitly on Section 232 costs - the first clearly attributed capacity consequence of this cycle, arriving a week before the next escalation. At the 22-September cash settlement of $3,242.00 the 50% leg alone is about $1,621.00/t.

THE Q4-2026 JAPANESE QUARTERLY PREMIUM SETTLEMENT - STILL THE LARGEST SINGLE DATED EVENT LEFT ON THIS PAGE AND NOW INSIDE TWO WEEKS. The pending range carried here is $280-310/t against a settled Q3 record of $395/t, a fall of 22-29% if it lands inside; it is unchanged for an EIGHTH consecutive run because no newer dated evidence has printed. THE BUYER'S CASE STRENGTHENED AGAIN THIS RUN AND IT IS NOW THE STRONGEST OF THE CYCLE: the exchange curve did not merely cross into contango, it DEEPENED to $22.00 on a second consecutive settled official while every other base metal moved towards immediacy. Alongside it sit producer offers of $310-325/t, Alba corroborated a third time at about 1.3 Mt, softer European premiums, and a central-China spot market transacting at a 70-90 yuan/mt discount to the October contract.

CHINA'S NATIONAL DAY HOLIDAY AND THE POST-HOLIDAY REBUILD TEST - THE CLEANEST FORWARD EXPERIMENT AVAILABLE ON CHINESE DEMAND. SMM attributes the current destocking - 12,000 tonnes from the prior Thursday, 55,000 tonnes from the prior Monday, national total reported below 800,000 tonnes - to a Xinjiang outbound shipment disruption and pre-holiday stockpiling, BOTH OF WHICH REVERSE BY DESIGN. The test is explicit: STRONG post-holiday operating rates that absorb the returning metal would mean the tightness was genuine; a MUTED return with inventory rebuilding would confirm it was seasonal and logistics-driven. The leading indicators point to the muted outcome - a central-China spot discount of 70-90 yuan/mt and a liquid-aluminium share that fell a further 0.02 percentage points on downstream production cuts. Note the one-to-two-week reporting lag on operating-rate surveys.

THE NEXT FEDERAL OPEN MARKET COMMITTEE MEETING, AND ITS RELEVANCE TO THIS PAGE IS NOW MORE QUALIFIED THAN IT WAS. With the dot plot revised to a 4.1% median for 2026 against 3.8% in June, and two meetings left in October and December, the projections imply at least one further increase before year-end. Carry acts on the curve rather than on the flat price, and the curve is where this page's central question sits. THE QUALIFICATION MATTERS: on the 22-September ring four of five other base-metal fronts moved TOWARDS immediacy under the same financing cost, so carry cannot be the whole explanation for aluminium's contango. A further increase would still argue against the contango reversing; a HOLD would remove the cleanest structural argument against a return to backwardation - but neither would settle the aluminium-specific residual.

THE Q3-2026 PEER REPORTING SEASON OPENS AND ENDS THE CURRENT LULL. No peer result has been reported in the last 48 hours and the most recent on this page remains Constellium's Q2 of 29-July. Q3 will be the first reporting period that spans the full post-restart Gulf picture, the 50% Section 232 regime in steady state, and a quarter in which the exchange price averaged materially above the first half - so it is the first genuine read on whether the margin expansion reported through H1 has persisted or has started to compress from the revenue side. The exchange price has now fallen on four of the last five settled sessions, which sharpens that question.

risks.text: THE CONTANGO MORE THAN DOUBLED ON A SECOND CONSECUTIVE OFFICIAL AND THE TREND IS HELD AT UP - THIS REMAINS THE PRIMARY RISK ON THE PAGE AND IT IS NOW BETTER EVIDENCED. The six-run sequence is $21.00, $18.50, $3.00, minus $10.50, minus $22.00: from the market paying a clear premium for immediate metal to paying more than twice as much to defer it. THIS PAGE PUBLISHED THE THREE-WAY TEST TWICE AND IT RESOLVED AGAINST THE TIGHTNESS CASE BOTH TIMES. WHAT IS NEW AND IMPORTANT IS THE CROSS-METAL EVIDENCE, AND IT CUTS AGAINST THIS PAGE'S OWN PREVIOUS EXPLANATION: on the identical ring copper's backwardation narrowed $58.00 to $37.00 and HELD, zinc's $87.00 to $68.00 and HELD, nickel's contango TIGHTENED $140.00 to $130.00 and lead's $38.00 to $26.50. Four of five fronts moved TOWARDS immediacy under the same financing cost. Carry is therefore a necessary condition and not a sufficient one, and the aluminium-specific residual is unexplained by any public evidence carried here. WHY UP AND NOT FLAT: a deepening is confirmation, and it came on a settled official rather than an indication. WHAT TURNS IT DOWN IS PUBLISHED: a return to backwardation beyond $15.00 on a settled official. TODAY'S 13:20 LONDON OFFICIAL IS THE THIRD READING.

THE FEDERAL RESERVE'S REVISED PATH IS STILL CONSISTENT WITH THE CURVE, BUT THE TREND IS CUT FROM UP TO FLAT BECAUSE TODAY'S BOARD WEAKENED THE CARRY ARGUMENT RATHER THAN STRENGTHENING IT. The Committee raised the target range 25 basis points to 3.75-4.00% on 16-September, unanimously at 12-0, and lifted its median 2026 federal funds projection from 3.8% in June to 4.1%, with 3.9% for 2027 and 3.6% for 2028; two meetings remain on the 2026 calendar. This page carries a nominal ten-year at about 4.958%, essentially unchanged, with real ten-year yields reported at 4.3-4.4%. A financing cost at that level is structurally hostile to a backwardation. THE PROBLEM WITH LEANING ON IT TODAY IS EMPIRICAL AND THIS PAGE WILL NOT HIDE IT: the same financing cost applies to copper, zinc, nickel and lead, and four of those five fronts moved TOWARDS immediacy on the 22-September ring while aluminium moved away. If carry were doing the work, the board would not look like that. DOWNGRADING THIS ARROW TO FLAT IS THE HONEST RESPONSE TO EVIDENCE THAT CUTS AGAINST A STORY THIS PAGE HAS BEEN TELLING, and it is preferable to quietly retaining the arrow and omitting the cross-metal table.

TARIFF POLICY IS NO LONGER ONLY SETTING REGIONAL PRICE - IT HAS STARTED REMOVING PHYSICAL CAPACITY, AND THE TREND IS RAISED TO UP ON A DATED, ATTRIBUTED EXAMPLE. The Section 232 headline rate is re-verified and UNCHANGED at 50% on articles and 25% on derivatives, with Annex I-C carve-outs at 15% for Japan, Korea, the UK, Switzerland, Taiwan and the EU; the 08-September annex lifting previously exempt downstream lines toward a combined 100% and Canada's 50% counter-tariffs across CAD 27.6bn remain in force. NO NEW INSTRUMENT PRINTED. WHAT IS NEW IS THE CONSEQUENCE: on 22-September Novelis was reported to be cutting production and about 80 jobs at Kingston, Ontario - roughly a third of that workforce - EXPLICITLY CITING THE COST OF THOSE TARIFFS on Canadian metal entering the United States. That is the first clearly attributed capacity reduction of this cycle, and it sits awkwardly against public forecasting that has the US Midwest premium averaging its highest-ever level in 2026 on the same rate: the policy is simultaneously lifting the US delivered price and removing North American conversion capacity. At the 22-September cash settlement of $3,242.00 the 50% leg alone is about $1,621.00/t, down $10.25/t on the session purely because the exchange price fell - the tariff leg is mechanical arithmetic on the exchange price, not a change in physical tightness. Next dated step: a US vehicle and dairy import ban on 29-September.

THE STOCK DRAWDOWN CONTINUED FOR A SECOND CONSECUTIVE SESSION, WHICH REMAINS THE CLEAREST PIECE OF GOOD NEWS FOR THE TIGHTNESS CASE - AND THE TREND IS HELD AT DOWN. Visible LME stock fell a further 75 tonnes to 242,125 on the 22-September session, a third draw in four sessions. SEVENTY-FIVE TONNES IS NOT A SIGNAL BY ITSELF AND THIS PAGE WILL NOT INFLATE IT: what matters is that the direction has been unchanged while the front travelled $43.00 in five sessions. Four of the five base-metal stock lines drew on the same ring, lead by 3,025 tonnes and zinc by 2,125, so aluminium's draw is not idiosyncratic. The level remains close to multi-decade lows and about 9,090 tonnes below the August monthly mean of 251,215. THE TENSION WITH THE CURVE IS UNRESOLVED AND HAS WIDENED: visible metal is still being consumed while the front pays progressively more to defer it, and no public evidence carried on this page reconciles the two. The chart floor is held at 235,000 with 7,125 tonnes of headroom and is re-checked every run.

THE GULF SUPPLY PICTURE REMAINS CONTESTED IN PUBLIC, BUT THE TREND IS CUT FROM FLAT TO DOWN BECAUSE THE FORWARD PACE IS NOW GUIDED TO SLOW. On the unwinding side the dated position strengthened: SMM's 23-September summary corroborates for a THIRD time in six days Aluminium Bahrain at about 1.3 million tonnes of recovered operating capacity, matching the CEO-sourced 18-September report of roughly 80% of a pre-war 1,623 kt plant with exports via Jeddah and Sohar; Emirates Global Aluminium's Al Taweelah remains a partial restart at a publicly stated 18% of capacity with a return guided for early 2027. AGAINST IT, CRU GROUP IS REPORTED AS HOLDING THAT GULF PRODUCTION IS DOWN AROUND 25% YEAR ON YEAR. Both cannot be fully right and this page will not quietly pick the one that fits its narrative; a figure that survives three separate public retellings without revision is nonetheless stronger evidence than a single report. WHAT IS NEW AND WHY THE ARROW TURNS DOWN: SMM states that while resumptions continued to ACCELERATE, SOME NEW PROJECTS WERE DELAYED and the pace of operating-capacity increases outside China is expected to SLOW in the coming months. The biggest single tranche is already in the market; less follows behind it than the restart list implies. The published deficit spread of 300,000-500,000 tonnes base against up to 1.4 million tonnes bull remains the honest encoding of the disagreement.

THE CHINESE DOWNSTREAM OVERHANG IS MARKED BACK TO UP THIS RUN, AND THE EVIDENCE IS A PRICE RATHER THAN AN INVENTORY. Central China transactions on 22-September settled around a DISCOUNT of 70-90 yuan/mt against the SHFE October contract, with SMM recording that downstream processing enterprises showed insufficient restocking willingness having already bought substantially at earlier low prices, and that suppliers preferred to reduce inventory ahead of the holiday rather than hold prices firm. A physical market transacting at a discount to the futures because buyers will not step up is a demand statement, not a logistics one. THE CONFIRMING NUMBER IS THE ONE THIS PAGE HAS TRACKED THROUGHOUT: the liquid-aluminium share FELL a further 0.02 percentage points on select downstream curtailments. If consumption were accelerating, liquid usage would rise. THE HONEST COUNTERWEIGHT: national ingot social inventory fell 12,000 tonnes on the week and 55,000 tonnes on the prior Monday, and South China held premiums of 210-250 yuan/mt on scarce domestic arrivals, with the national ingot total now reported below 800,000 tonnes - but the named drivers of the draw are a Xinjiang rail disruption and pre-holiday restocking, both of which reverse by design. The post-holiday operating rates are the test.

THE COST FLOOR HAS STOPPED FALLING HARD AND THE TREND IS RAISED FROM DOWN TO FLAT - BUT THE CARBON DATA GAP IS THE LARGER HALF OF THIS RISK AND IT IS NOW SIX RUNS OLD. Brent fell a fifth consecutive session but only 0.62% to about $99.71, against 3.77% the day before; European gas TTF fell 1.83% to about EUR 71.91, against 7.90%. The complex has gone from falling hard to drifting, which materially weakens the case for a sharply lower carbon settlement when one finally prints. THE GAS MOVE STILL TRANSMITS FASTEST, through European smelter power, and continues to relieve the two named gas exposures here - Alunorte's TEMPORARY gas-supplier terminal-access agreement and Qatalum's curtailment at roughly 60% of 648 kt nameplate on reduced gas - as well as improving Slovalco's restart economics. THE CARBON COMPLEX IS THE REAL GAP: prebaked anodes, coal tar pitch and green petcoke normally settle around the 17th-18th of the month and NO NEW PUBLIC SETTLEMENT HAS PRINTED for a sixth consecutive run, so roughly a fifth of cash cost is carried on marks about a month old. No history has been appended on an interpolated basis and none will be. THE SECOND-ORDER POINT CUTS THE OTHER WAY FROM THE OBVIOUS ONE: a falling cost floor lowers marginal-cost support under the price, so a basket that has stopped falling is mildly supportive rather than bearish.

THE Q4-2026 JAPANESE PREMIUM SETTLEMENT IS NOW THE LARGEST UNPRICED SINGLE EVENT ON THIS PAGE AND THE TREND IS RAISED TO UP BECAUSE THE BUYER'S CASE STRENGTHENED MATERIALLY THIS RUN. The premium panel is carried for a fourth consecutive run - no price-reporting agency publishes into a 03:50 London window - and the oldest material carry is the CIF Japan spot indication at $370/t against dated September spot reporting of roughly $320-380/t and producer offers of $310-325/t for October-December shipments. The settled Q3 benchmark of $395/t is not stale, because a quarterly benchmark is fixed until the quarter turns, but it is increasingly disconnected. THE PENDING RANGE ON THIS PAGE IS $280-310/t, a fall of 22-29%, and it is unchanged for an eighth consecutive run because no newer dated evidence has printed. WHAT CHANGED IS THE NEGOTIATING BACKDROP: the exchange curve has not merely crossed into contango but DEEPENED to $22.00 on a second consecutive settled official, while every other metal on the board moved towards immediacy. That is the strongest buyer-side argument of this cycle and it carries a settlement price rather than a view. A reader looking only at the panel would see no warning in the numbers; the warning is written here.

STRAIT OF HORMUZ AND REGIONAL SHIPPING DISRUPTION IS CUT FROM UP TO FLAT, AND THE REASON IS A GENUINE CHANGE IN THE NEWS FLOW RATHER THAN A CHANGE ON THE WATER. SMM's 23-September summary records that on 22-September President Trump, at the 81st UN General Assembly, reiterated the United States would reach an agreement with Iran AFTER THE NOVEMBER MIDTERM ELECTIONS; that Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi met US envoy Witkoff in New York, with Trump describing a three-hour meeting with the Iranian delegation as very productive and another to be arranged; and that Iran has publicly set CONDITIONS for reopening the Strait - immediate lifting of the maritime blockade, immediate unfreezing of all Iranian assets, and an end to the war on all regional fronts. THIS IS THE FIRST GENUINE DE-ESCALATION SIGNAL OF THIS CYCLE AND IT DESERVES TO MOVE THE ARROW. IT DOES NOT DESERVE TO MOVE IT TO DOWN. The stated US timetable falls after November; Iran's conditions are maximalist; and nothing operational has changed. The prior evidence stands unrefuted: Reuters tracking cited 20-September put daily commodity transits at 3-6 ships between 2 and 18 September against a normal ten-day average of 12-18, and a tanker was reportedly struck near Khasab, Oman on 18-September with attribution still UNCONFIRMED. The second-order freight evidence also stands: Guinea-to-China ocean freight at $39-42/wmt on a lane that never touches the Strait. TREAT THESE AS REPORTED DIPLOMATIC STATEMENTS, NOT SETTLED OUTCOMES.

THE EX-CHINA RESTART PIPELINE IS VISIBLE AND DATED BUT THE TREND IS HELD AT FLAT, AND THE REASON IS THAT IT GOT SLOWER AND LARGER AT THE SAME TIME. The publicly reported list carries Aluminium Bahrain at about 1.3 Mt annualised against a 1,623 kt plant, now corroborated by a THIRD source in six days, with SMM's 23-September summary explicitly framing it as further lifting ex-China operating capacity; Century's Mt Holly at full capacity for the first time since 2015 on a $50m investment restarting more than 50,000 t; Slovalco restarting the first 75,000 t of 175,000 t guided for Q4-2026, with its power input having moved favourably again as European gas fell 7.90%; Magnitude 7 Metals with a first potline guided before end-2026 for about 75,000 t, publicly attributed to the 50% US tariff; and EGA's DX+ Ultra licence to NALCO for a proposed 500,000 t/y Angul expansion. AGAINST THAT, SMM NOW GUIDES THAT SOME NEW PROJECTS WERE DELAYED AND THE PACE OF OPERATING-CAPACITY INCREASES WILL SLOW IN COMING MONTHS - and separately, US Section 232 has begun REMOVING North American conversion capacity, with Novelis cutting production at Kingston, Ontario. Restarts are slow, none of this lands this quarter, and the two new pieces of evidence point in opposite directions. Flat is the honest arrow. ADDED THIS RUN: Azerbaijan announced a national mining and metallurgy programme on 23-September targeting 100,000 t/y of aluminium by 2030 - recorded because announcements of this kind accumulate, but weighted as small, since 100,000 tonnes is roughly 0.14% of global primary output and 2030 is beyond any horizon carried here. China's Ministry of Natural Resources separately named ALUMINIUM among the scarce minerals targeted under the 15th Five-Year Plan, which is a long-dated resource-security signal rather than a near-term supply one.

EU CARBON-BORDER COST IS A SLOW, STRUCTURAL RISK TO EUROPEAN DELIVERED PRICE AND IT IS ADDED TO THE REGISTER THIS RUN AT FLAT. SMM analysis published 22-September, using Eurostat Comext data updated 15-September, shows extra-EU aluminium foil imports (HS7607) at 137.28 kt in January-July 2026, DOWN 22.2% year on year, with theoretical net certificate exposure for identified non-exempt origins down 24.1% to 326.74 kt CO2e. YET TRADE-WEIGHTED UNIT EXPOSURE ROSE 0.7%, from 2.6377 to 2.6550 t CO2e per tonne, because the origin mix shifted: China and Turkiye together now account for 75.8% of calculable exposure against 69.7% a year earlier, and China's default net unit exposure of 4.5559 t CO2e/t is about 2.5 times Turkiye's 1.8191. WHY IT IS FLAT RATHER THAN UP: the mechanism is known, the parameters are published, and nothing accelerated this run - aluminium carries a 10% mark-up in 2026 against a 97.5% CBAM factor, and certificate prices are EUR 75.36 for Q1 and EUR 75.28 for Q2 with Q3 unpublished as of 18-September. THE USEFUL WARNING IS METHODOLOGICAL: falling import volumes do not establish that unit carbon-cost exposure has eased, and a 'low-carbon' label is not a substitute for installation-level verified data.

THE BALANCE VIEW IS UNCHANGED AND THE 11-SEPTEMBER DATA SHARPENS THE CENTRAL PUZZLE RATHER THAN RESOLVING IT: global primary production was reported down 1.7% year on year at 6.16 million tonnes and GCC output down 44% year on year in July to 293,000 tonnes from 523,000 - a genuine, large supply loss. YET China's August exports were 626,000 tonnes, taking January-August to 4.67 million tonnes, up 16.7% year on year, and dated commentary describes Middle Eastern and Australian ingot supply into Japan as RELATIVELY AMPLE with Asian premiums collapsing toward a $280-290 Q4 consensus. A DEFICIT IN PRIMARY UNITS CAN COEXIST WITH AMPLE REGIONAL AVAILABILITY IF THE RELIEVING METAL ARRIVES AS CHINESE SEMI-FINISHED AND ALLOY PRODUCT THAT NEVER PASSES THROUGH AN LME WAREHOUSE - which is the most coherent published explanation for why a multi-decade exchange inventory low, a widening backwardation and collapsing physical premiums are all true at once.

The published restart schedule is the reason, and it gained another dated entry on 20-August. Nanshan Aluminum's 2026 semi-annual report confirms 250,000 t/y of Indonesian aluminium and 260,000 t/y of carbon under construction at Bintan Industrial Park, with the integrated anode carbon removing one of the genuine physical constraints on commissioning new non-Chinese capacity. Alongside it: Gulf pre-incident output guided for Q1-2027 and running faster than the market expected; Slovalco 75,000 t/y from Q4-2026; Magnitude 7 Metals 75,000 t/y before year-end; Mount Holly already at full capacity and lifting US primary output by close to 10%; the Australian smelter's power secured to 2038 removing a closure risk over up to 590,000 t/y; Alunorte back at full rate; and a 500,000 t/y integrated Saudi greenfield through all compliance approvals with construction under way. These are published commitments with dates attached rather than projections, which is why the deficit is expected to narrow rather than persist at 2026 scale.
